chapter_title: Concerning the Form of the Word, that [ ... 30 ...
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** The formation of truth as it proceeds from the interior will and becomes perceptible to the [GAP-1] receptive understanding of others. [GAP-2] The deeper volition draws it upward from within, and the understanding unfolds it into intelligible form, and the natural rational faculty distinguishes and defines it into discrete ideas, and the outermost sensory comprehension gathers it into completeness. Thus truth comes forth through the operation of these five successive degrees of the mind and is perceived in the external life.

**¶2:** In like manner, a truth of genuine spiritual worth: One agency pours forth the initial influx from within, and another shapes it through the labor of reformation, and another refines and orders it as it is turned through successive states, and another impresses upon it the authentic image of the Divine, and another purifies it by separating what is genuine from what is counterfeit. [GAP-3] Behold, these five successive spiritual operations shape and perfect [GAP-4] their truth of communicable worth, and it enters into the life of the spiritual community. It becomes a living good capable of being received into the understanding and given forth through charity.

**¶3:** This is also the nature of truth proceeding from the Divine: it is formed and perfected through five successive degrees of the interior life. It comes forth and is perceived by the [GAP-5] receptive faculties of others.

---

*Note: The fivefold structure in both images — members of speech and craftsmen of the coin — corresponds to the same reality: truth descends through five discrete degrees from its origin in the will toward its outermost communicable form. The "coin" — a unit of value that circulates — is truth rendered into a form that can serve the mutual exchange of spiritual life, which is charity itself.*

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The production of the word t[hat comes] from the mouth and is heard by the [ears]. [The mouth shapes it] and the throat draws it up and the tongue spreads it out and the teeth cut it and the lips g[at]her it! The word shall come forth through the power of th[ese five] members and be heard outside.

Simila[rly] the coin: One shall pour it out and an [othe]r beat it and another trim it as it is turned, and a[nother] put the stamp on it and another wipe it in the sieve (?). [Behold], these five craftsmen shall shape and beautify [their] coin, and it comes amongst mankind. It becomes a posse[ssion] to be received and given.
This is also the case with the [wor]d, as it is formed and embellished by five [member]s. It comes forth and is heard by the ears [of] others.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading renders this as "receptive understanding of others," and in the natural-plane vocabulary of speech, the ears are the organ of reception/hearing — perfectly matching the text's "is heard by the ears."

The text names four members (throat, tongue, teeth, lips) but states "these five members" — the fifth must be the mouth, already introduced as the origin of the word; its shaping action begins the enumeration that continues with "and the throat draws it up," corresponding to the spiritual reading's first degree where truth proceeds from the interior will.
The spiritual reading confirms "Behold" as the demonstrative exclamation introducing the summary statement; this is a standard Kephalaia formula for drawing attention to a completed enumeration.
The possessive "their" correctly refers back to the five craftsmen who collectively produce the coin, confirmed by the spiritual reading's "their truth of communicable worth."
The preposition "of" is grammatically required to form "by the ears of others," matching the spiritual reading's "receptive faculties of others."
